rules.statement: Rotate a credential by adding the replacement beside the rotated one in one unit of work, so both authenticate until the old one expires or is deleted; never remove the rotated credential in the same operation.
rules.why: Removing the rotated secret in the same change breaks every caller that holds it until it is reconfigured; create, switch, delete lets the holder switch while the old secret still works.
rules.check: Look for rotate/replace code paths that delete, revoke or overwrite the existing secret while they create the new one, or that replace key material in place.

rules.statement: When a rotation sets a grace expiry on the rotated credential, use the earlier of its current expiry and the requested value, clamp it to no earlier than the credential's creation, bound the credential's activation and retirement times with it, and leave the expiry unchanged when no value is given.
rules.why: Rotation must never extend a credential's lifetime. A past value stops the secret at once, and the grace bound keeps a forgotten delete from leaving a stale credential accepted forever.
rules.check: Check grace-expiry assignment for a min with the existing expiry, a clamp to the creation time, adjustment of the active window, and no change when the value is omitted. Flag any path that can push an expiry later.

rules.statement: When resolving a client's credentials for authentication, drop every secret whose expiry is not after now before deserializing or using it, so that every client authentication method honors expiry.
rules.why: An overlap bounded by expiry only works when a credential past its ExpiresWhen stops authenticating, and that applies to every credential, including a by-value key.
rules.check: Look at the code that loads client secrets for authentication. Flag a missing expiry filter, a filter that uses `<` where it should use `<=` against now, or a filter that covers only some authentication methods or runs after deserialization.

rules.statement: A generated shared client secret must have at least 256 bits of entropy, taken from a single shared policy constant. Generators throw below that floor, and API endpoints answer 400 for a request below it.
rules.why: The secrets ADR sets a floor on generated secret entropy, and every generated shared secret has to meet it.
rules.check: Look for shared-secret generation or create/registration endpoints that take an entropy or size argument without checking it against the shared minimum constant, or that hard-code a different value.

rules.statement: Don't reuse a stored shared secret's encoded length (such as the UTF-8 length of its base64url string) as entropy when generating a replacement. Derive the entropy by inverting the encoding (bytes * 3/4 * 8 for base64url), with the minimum entropy floor as the lower bound.
rules.why: Copying the stored size as the replacement's entropy would grow the secret on every rotation.
rules.check: Check that replacement-generation code that reads KeySizeBits or a stored length and passes it straight to the generator as entropy converts it from the encoded length first.

rules.statement: Authorize and audit a composite operation as the primitive operations it performs. For a rotation that is create and update, never delete. Audit the update only when a value actually changed, and never include secret material in audit records.
rules.why: Rotation performs a create and an update, so the caller needs exactly those permissions, and the audit trail must reflect what changed without leaking material.
rules.check: Look at authorization checks and audit events in composite secret operations. Flag permission checks that don't match the operations performed, audit events emitted when nothing changed, and audit payloads that contain material.

rules.statement: When a mutating endpoint accepts an If-Match header, compare it with the target resource's concurrency token, and answer 412 on a mismatch or when another request changed the data after this one read it.
rules.why: This prevents a stale or concurrent request from silently overwriting a change.
rules.check: Look for mutating endpoints that ignore a sent If-Match header, compare it against the wrong resource's token, or let a concurrency conflict at save time surface as something other than 412.

rules.statement: An endpoint that creates a secret returns 201 Created with the new material only in that response body, and marks the response uncacheable.
rules.why: A secret is revealed once and never cached.
rules.check: Check secret-creating endpoints for a status other than 201, missing no-store cache headers, or material appearing in other responses or resources.

rules.statement: Never generate an asymmetric key pair on the server on behalf of a client. Rotating a client-held key answers 400, and the client imports the new key and deletes the old one itself.
rules.why: The server would otherwise hold a private key that the client owns.
rules.check: Look for rotate or generate paths that create private keys for client credentials, or that accept a rotate request for an asymmetric secret type without rejecting it with 400.
